transcript.content: Hello, I’m Dr. ____. What brings you in today?

Hi, Doctor. It's really nice to meet you. Am I doing this right? Just start talking? Okay, great. 

Well, um, my job actually asked me to come see you. I do general maintenance and repair work, and I'm usually really eager to help everyone out. I try so hard to do a good job for them. But lately... well, it's a little embarrassing, honestly. I don't want you to think I'm a bad employee or anything, because I really do care. But I guess I've been having a little trouble with, um, forgetting some scheduled callbacks, and... some work orders. Even just basic follow-ups I promised people I'd take care of. 

I always mean to do them, I really do! But it just sort of piled up on me so much recently. My boss noticed, and they actually sent me here because I'm up for a promotion, and they want me to get this sorted out before I lose my shot at moving up. Does that make sense? I hope I'm explaining it okay.
Did these attention and forgetfulness problems start back in childhood?

Oh, um... well, I guess so, yes. I hope it's okay to admit that. I mean, it wasn't terrible or anything, I was always a really good kid! My teachers always told my parents I was bright and sweet. But... yeah, I suppose even back in grade school, way before I had all these work orders to juggle, I was kind of like this. 

I'd, um, misplace my assignments a lot, or I'd only hear the first half of the directions and kind of miss the rest. The teachers had to give me little reminders to actually finish my classwork instead of just staring out the window. I really tried my best, though, I promise! Is that the kind of thing you mean?
When you were in school, did you have a lot of trouble learning to read, write, or do math compared with other kids?

Oh, no, I wouldn't say I had trouble learning those things! I was actually pretty good at the subjects themselves. I mean, I hope it doesn't sound like I'm bragging, but I understood the material fine. 

It was really just the... the keeping track of things, like I mentioned. The reading and writing and math were okay, as long as I could actually get myself to sit still and focus on them for long enough. Does that make sense? I definitely didn't need any special help with learning how to do the work itself, I promise. I just... struggled a little with the organization part. Is that what you were asking?
Have you ever had ongoing problems with deliberately breaking rules or getting into fights, hurting people or animals, stealing, lying, or destroying property?

Oh, goodness, no! No, never anything like that. I would never want to hurt anyone or break the rules. I've always tried really hard to be polite and do what I'm supposed to do. 

I mean, I'd feel just awful if I ever caused trouble like stealing or fighting. I'm really a very peaceful person, and I love animals! I've never been in any kind of trouble with the law or anything like that, I promise. I hope you don't think I'm that kind of person just because I've been a little forgetful lately. I always try to be a good person, is that... does that answer your question okay?
Do you also find yourself feeling very restless or unable to sit still?

Oh, um... no, not really. I mean, I hope it's okay to say this, but I'm actually pretty good at sitting still when I need to! I'm not the type to be bouncing off the walls or anything. 

At work, if I'm fixing a plumbing issue or working on an electrical panel, I can stay right there until it's done. I might lose my screwdriver a few times while I'm doing it, but I'm not... you know, running around or feeling like I have a motor inside me. I try very hard to be respectful in meetings and sit quietly, too. I mean, maybe I'll shift in my chair a little or tap my foot, but just normal things, right? Nothing disruptive. I hope that's what you were looking for?
